notes: Transcribed from the General Catalog History program page. Three lower-division courses plus twelve four-unit upper-division courses. The distribution inside those twelve — field of emphasis (3+), non-field (3+), pre-1800 period (3), colloquium (1, numbered 160-190) — overlaps itself, so it is carried as prose on the upper-division bucket rather than as separate buckets that would double-count a single course. At least eight of the twelve must be taken at UC San Diego, and at most two units of HIxx 199 may count.

buckets.label: Lower-Division History
buckets.note: Any three lower-division history courses. The Revelle Humanities sequence or Eleanor Roosevelt's Making of the Modern World sequence may be substituted — the department accepts those in place of these three.

buckets.label: The Craft of History
buckets.note: Required of every history major, and normally taken early in the upper-division sequence.

buckets.label: Upper-Division History
buckets.note: Eleven further four-unit upper-division courses (twelve including HITO 100). Within them: at least three in your field of emphasis, at least three outside it, three on periods before 1800, and at least one colloquium numbered 160-190 with a substantial term paper. Eight of the twelve must be taken at UC San Diego; at most two units of 199 count.

buckets.label: Language and Overseas Study (Global Relations emphasis only)
buckets.note: Only students in the Global Relations field of emphasis carry this: eight overseas credits plus proficiency in a second language. Not checkable here — confirm with the department.
